stories.title: Trump says new Iran talks set to start, calls off strikes
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said that new negotiations with Iran will begin today after he decided to hold off on striking the Islamic republic to pursue a deal to end the war. Mr Trump told reporters that the talks would cover the Strait of Hormuz - a route for global energy supplies that has become a key sticking point in the conflict - and, ultimately, the denuclearisation of Iran. For its part, Iran said it was nearing a deal with Oman over a new route through the strait, where yesterday a tanker reported an explosion nearby, underscoring the continued volatility of the strategic waterway. Washington and Tehran have been at war since 28 February, when the US and Israel launched surprise strikes against Iran, though months of on-off diplomacy have led to periods of relative calm.

stories.title: Man, 50s, dies in incident off Castletownbere Pier
stories.summary: A man in his 50s has died after getting into difficulty in the water at Castletownbere Pier in West Cork. Shortly after 5.30pm, Valentia Coastguard was alerted to a report by the National Ambulance Service that a man was in the water at the pier. The local coastguard, along with the RNLI's all-weather lifeboat were dispatched to the scene. The man was taken from the water in an unresponsive state and was pronounced dead at the scene.

stories.title: Ceuta crisis puts Ireland's EU presidency to the test
stories.summary: Of all the potential flashpoints that risked overshadowing the first weeks of Ireland's EU presidency, it is safe to say Ceuta was until recently not one. The tiny Spanish territory on the north African coastline has long been a source of dispute in the region. But with Aughinish Alumina, ongoing calls for a possible EU-wide version of the occupied territories bill, social media age restrictions and domestic political matters, only the best of predictors would have suggested the autonomous location just 18.5km in size was going to garner much attention. All of that changed this week when a sudden influx of Moroccan migrants into Ceuta pushed the area directly into an EU spotlight which is unlikely to dim any time soon.

stories.summary: But this year, it is hard to see how much more the country's firefighters, and the communities impacted, can endure. However, it was over the past 10 days that the country faced its most difficult period. "Completely unprecedented," is how French President Emmanuel Macron described the vast wildfire that raged in the country’s south-west Gironde region.

The Tribeswomen beat Kerry 2-07 to 0-12 in Croke Park on Sunday with Leanne Coen scoring two superb goals for just their second ever All-Ireland title. "There's a lot of pressure from the outside. You know always the question of why Galway haven't been able to do it and some of these girls have soldiered for 13, 14, 15 years. See the likes of Louise (Ward) and Nicola (Ward) and Olivia (Divilly). There's so many and to finally, finally get that one cup that was missing for them, I'm so thrilled. Delighted." Many had predicted that the game would be an attacking fest with both sides known for their free-flowing football this season. Galway had a 16 point average winning margin from their last four games.

stories.title: Maunsell stars as Abbeydorney win Kerry hurling title
stories.summary: Oisín Maunsell starred with 2-04 as Abbeydorney were crowned Kerry senior hurling champions for a third year in-a-row after overcoming a determined St Brendan's side in a one-sided 3-16 to 1-12 contest before a large crowd in Austin Stack Park. The Neilus Flynn Cup will now make the short trip back up the R556 and 'Odorney’ can now look forward to the Munster Intermediate Club Championship where they play the Waterford Intermediate champions in November. While it is their forwards that will make the headlines, scoring all 3-16 of Abbeydorney's final tally between them, an impressive defensive display that limited St Brendan's to just 1-8 from play was the baseline for their historic three-in-a-row victory. Goals from Michael Slattery and Oisín Maunsell were the difference as Abbeydorney took a seven-point lead – 2-07 to 0-06 – into the half time break, before Maunsell got a second for the Kerry champions as the men in black and amber outscored their Ardfert counterparts by 1-09 to 1-06 in the second half.

stories.title: Skinner leaves role as Manchester United head coach
stories.summary: Marc Skinner has left his role as Manchester United head coach by mutual agreement after five years at the helm of the club. Skinner had another year to run on his contract but has decided to move on a month out from United beginning their Women's Super League season at London City Lionesses on 4 September. Under Skinner, who succeeded Casey Stoney in July 2021, United reached four domestic cup finals in as many seasons, winning the club’s first major honour in women’s football with the 2024 FA Cup triumph. "Marc Skinner has departed his role as head coach of Manchester United Women by mutual agreement," a club statement said on Monday.

stories.title: inside The Centre Culturel Irlandais: where Ireland & Europe meet
stories.summary: As Ireland assumes the Presidency of the Council of the European Union, the Centre Culturel Irlandais in Paris presents an ambitious autumn and winter programme of exhibitions, debates, theatre and music. The CCI's Rosetta Beaugendre reflects on the Centre's ongoing role as a cultural bridge between Ireland and Europe. Modern Ireland owes much to the European Union, born itself in the aftermath of conflict and out of a desire to avoid history being repeated. The country's attachment since 1973 to seeking common ground found concrete expression nearly 25 years ago when the Centre Culturel Irlandais was inaugurated in one of the world's finest cultural capitals, in the heart of Europe, in the former Irish College. This elegant 18th century building had after all concentrated the learning, the hopes and maturing of generations of young Irishmen on the Continent. In 2002, although not yet 30, I felt the resonance of this confident even audacious affirmation of Ireland’s place in the European story. Now, in 2026, as the country takes over the presidency of the Council of the EU, we are on the threshold of a season of ambitious events and collaborations led by our inspired director, Nora Hickey M'Sichili. The CCI could be considered the undiplomatic diplomats of the party, teasing out the kind of issues that Fintan O’Toole has dubbed in the past 'unknown knowns’. For instance, our rentrée exhibition looks at Ireland’s housing crisis and, as such, provides a conduit for Irish citizens’ concerns that have filtered through the percolator of artists’ psyches and practices to be expressed in material form. Everyone Should Have a Home explores frustrations, contradictions, grey areas but equally includes proposals for innovative 21st century housing. In addition, we have teamed up with Marsh’s Library to present a timely exhibition Gulliver 300, in our Old Library, that highlights the continuing relevance of Swift’s critique of human nature, societal norms and flaws… one need only think of the satirist’s 'Modest Proposal’ in response to overcrowding in Dublin’s 18th century tenements!

stories.title: Buffalo Traffic Jam: best pals, one of 2026's best albums
stories.summary: As life 180s go, things have worked out brilliantly for Buffalo Traffic Jam's Frankie Cassidy and Nathan Ross. Right about now, the 2025 graduates in architecture (Cassidy) and mechanical engineering (Ross) should be climbing the first rungs on the corporate ladder. Instead, the best friends who first met during an epic night of Mario Kart at Montana State University, became roommates, devoured other people's songs in between hitting the books, and then started writing and recording their own, have made one of the best debut albums of the year - and sold out two April 2027 shows at Dublin's National Stadium before its release. "We didn't play our first gig together until 2024 at a local Montana venue called The Filling Station," smiles Cassidy as he bashfully tries to get his head around the past two years. "That was our first time we ever played live."

stories.title: Thousands attend Bray Air Display in Wicklow
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people have attended this year's Bray Air Display, the 19th edition of Ireland’s biggest aviation event. It featured Team Raven, one of the biggest civilian air display teams in the world along with parachutists from the Defence Forces Black Knight team, wing walkers and historic aircraft. There is a Future of Flight zone where virtual reality headsets let people experience what it is like to pilot a drone and in real life drone displays. A small fire in a green area between the beach at Bray and Bray head was extinguished quickly this afternoon before the Bray Air Display started and did not have any impact on the event.

stories.title: Labour's Bev Craig elected mayor of Greater Manchester
stories.summary: The UK's ruling Labour Party comfortably retained the mayoralty of Greater Manchester following an election triggered by new Prime Minister Andy Burnham's return to parliament. Bev Craig, the leader of Manchester City Council, was elected after winning 47.15% of the votes in the first round. The anti-immigration Reform UK party, which had been riding high in national polls, came in second place with a 21% share. Without the 50% of votes needed to win outright, the counting proceeded to a second round.

stories.title: Bank of Ireland's H1 pre-tax profits jump 33% to €960m
stories.summary: Bank of Ireland has reported a 33% jump in pre-tax profits for the six months to the end of June and said it was upgrading its guidance for the full year. Bank of Ireland said its half year pre-tax profits rose to €960m, and it also announced an interim dividend of 39 cent per share, an increase of 56%. Lending during the six month period rose by 4% to €84 billion. Bank of Ireland noted an "excellent" performance in its Irish lending which rose by €2.2 billion - up 7% - but it saw a fall of €0.5 billion in its UK lending where it said it prioritised value over volume.

stories.title: Ospreys or Scarlets face axe as WRU outlines cut plans
stories.summary: Wales are to go ahead with plans to cut their number of professional franchises from four to three, spelling the end for either the Ospreys or Scarlets, both former winners of the United Rugby Championship. The Welsh Rugby Union on Wednesday confirmed the proposed change to the professional game and plans to establish three men's teams from the 2028/29 season – one based in the capital, one in west Wales and one in east Wales. Cardiff, owned by the Welsh Rugby Union, and Dragons, an independently backed business, are set to be given licences, leaving Swansea-based Ospreys and Llanelli-based Scarlets to compete for the remaining spot. Ospreys have won the URC, in its previous guise, four times, most recently in 2012.

stories.title: RTÉ Supporting the Arts this August
stories.summary: From major festivals and theatrical premieres to exhibitions, concerts and family-friendly celebrations, audiences nationwide are invited to experience the richness and diversity of Ireland's cultural landscape throughout the month. National Heritage Week returns with hundreds of events taking place across Ireland, encouraging people of all ages to explore and celebrate the country’s rich natural, built and cultural heritage. Through guided tours, exhibitions, talks, workshops and community initiatives, Heritage Week continues to foster a deeper appreciation of Ireland’s shared history and traditions. August brings a number of exciting productions to the Abbey Theatre. Highlights include Ulster American, starring Matthew Broderick, running on the Abbey Stage from 12 to 22 August 2026, a sharp satirical comedy exploring identity, privilege and power. Later in the month, Mirandolina, Marina Carr's adaptation of Carlo Goldoni's La Locandiera, opens on 28 August, marking its Irish premiere as part of an international co-production. Kilkenny Arts Festival returns this August with an ambitious multidisciplinary programme featuring music, theatre, literature, visual arts and performance. Widely regarded as one of Ireland’s premier arts festivals, it attracts leading Irish and international artists while transforming the city into a vibrant cultural hub.

stories.title: Met Gala 2027 will honour controversial designer John Galliano
stories.summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that its next exhibition will celebrate the career of John Galliano, whose renowned stint as the Creative Director at Dior ended after he was filmed making antisemitic and racist remarks outside a Paris cafe in 2011. John Galliano: Horizons will be on display at The Met from May 9, 2027 until January 9, 2028, and will be a career-spanning look at a figure largely regarded by the fashion industry as one of the most influential designers of the last number of decades. The exhibition will be kicked off by the annual Met Gala on 3 May, where the A-list attendees will be sure to pay homage to Galliano's work. With this exhibit, Galliano becomes only the third living designer to have their work featured in a solo exhibition by the institute, after Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo of Comme des Garçons in 2017.

stories.title: Israel conveys 'concerns' to US on Gaza peace plan
stories.summary: Israel has conveyed concerns to the United States on a Gaza plan hailed by President Donald Trump, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said. Citing Hamas officials, media outlets on Friday reported that Hamas agreed to the plan but the group has not officially commented.

stories.title: High Court finds Tusla in contempt of court
stories.summary: The High Court has found the Child and Family Agency Tusla is in contempt of court for failing to provide secure placements for vulnerable children despite being directed to do so. Legal sources say it is believed to be the first time a State agency has been held to be in contempt of court. The action was taken on behalf of three children in respect of whom special care orders were made by the High Court. Ms Justice Emily Egan said even though these children had now received placements, it was a systemic and recurring problem and there were still five to seven children every week for whom no special care beds were available despite orders being made.

stories.title: Aer Lingus posts half-year loss of €34m ahead of job cuts
stories.summary: Aer Lingus has reported an operating loss of €34m for the first half of 2026 compared to an operating profit of €80m the same time last year. Earlier this month Aer Lingus said that up to 500 jobs could be cut at the airline due to a planned 6% reduction in its flight capacity. Under the cost-cutting plan, 290 roles are under threat in head office functions, along with 140 cabin roles and 70 pilot positions. Aer Lingus said today that its costs increased by 8% in the first half of the year and passenger revenue decreased by 3%.

stories.title: Spain says migrant crossings into Ceuta stopped overnight
stories.summary: Spain has said that migrant crossings into its North African territory of Ceuta stopped overnight, as police began installing a 500-metre floating barrier off its border with Morocco. It comes after around 60,000 people crossed from Morocco into Ceuta by land and sea from Thursday, in an unprecedented surge at one of the European Union's only land borders with Africa. At least 67 people died in the attempt, according to Spain's Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska. More than 48,000 migrants have returned to Morocco within 48 hours without major incident, Spain said.

stories.title: Tyrrell: Final ref Farrelly got two big calls 'spot on'
stories.summary: The dramatic end to the All-Ireland women's senior final had amateur rulesfolk thumbing through well worn versions of the LGFA rulebook trying to make sense of what exactly went down in those frantic final moments. Kerry star Síofra O’Shea first looked to have drawn her side level late in the game – before that score was chalked off as play was brought back for a two-point free attempt following the loss of an 'advantage’ for the Kingdom ladies. Amazingly, O’Shea then appeared to have won the game in the most dramatic fashion when her two-point attempt dipped in under Galway keeper Leah O’Halloran’s crossbar for an apparent goal. However, that score was quickly ruled out as well as referee Maggie Farrelly had signalled for a square ball.
